usage.callShape: POST https://makespdf.com/api/v1/render with JSON body {templateId, data}
usage.outputShape: Raw binary PDF (application/pdf, ~53KB). paid_fetch/qa-pay surfaces it as a 'base64:...' string body; strip the 'base64:' prefix and decode to get the PDF bytes. Response headers carry x-pages (page count) and x-render-ms.
quirks: Response body is a raw binary PDF, not JSON — surfaced as a 'base64:...' string by paid_fetch/qa-pay; strip the 'base64:' prefix and base64-decode to obtain the PDF bytes.
Body must supply EITHER templateId (curated/saved template) OR dsl (Builder DSL script) — they are mutually exclusive — plus a data object whose keys fill the template's {{placeholders}}.

Get valid templateIds from GET /api/v1/templates?owner=library (free GET). Verified IDs include certificate-modern, certificate-formal, invoice-classic/compact/modern, letter-business/personal, quote-classic/modern.
Sibling endpoint /api/v1/markdown ($0.01) takes GitHub-Flavoured Markdown {markdown, options} for simple docs; /api/v1/render ($0.02) is for template/DSL-based branded/compliant layouts.
Output is PDF/UA-1 + PDF/A-2A compliant (tagged, accessible).
usage.guide: POST to https://makespdf.com/api/v1/render with a JSON body containing a templateId plus a data object filling that template's placeholders. Pick a templateId from the free GET https://makespdf.com/api/v1/templates?owner=library (e.g. certificate-modern, invoice-modern, letter-business). Payment of $0.02 USDC on Base is automatic via x402. The response is a synchronous raw binary PDF (application/pdf); paid_fetch delivers it as a 'base64:...' string, so strip the prefix and base64-decode to get the PDF bytes. For simple Markdown-to-PDF use the cheaper /api/v1/markdown endpoint with {markdown, options} instead.
